subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status health be sourced from the live gateway runtime, from a new passive local plugin status contract, or should current `not checked` behavior be accepted for this class?
rationale: The remaining fix changes a user-visible diagnostic contract and the plugin-runtime loading boundary; source inspection shows the bug class remains, but the permanent owner boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Use live gateway runtime health
options.body: Make deep/status-all human and JSON status consume gateway memory runtime health when local materialization is inconclusive, and keep embedding readiness as a separate degraded detail.

options.title: Add passive plugin status contract
options.body: Define an explicit plugin API for cheap side-effect-free memory status and update external plugin docs/tests before using it in status.

options.title: Accept not-checked mitigation
options.body: Keep current status behavior, close or retire the conflicting fork PR, and fold any remaining work into the broader canonical issue only if maintainers do not want live runtime health in status.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway runtime health
recommendation.body: Make deep/status-all human and JSON status consume gateway memory runtime health when local materialization is inconclusive, and keep embedding readiness as a separate degraded detail.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame and feature-history trail point to steipete as the strongest owner of the status/memory-runtime boundary and recent status behavior.
